purpose: Research-backed instrument behavior layer for the AI Composition program.
tuning_reference: A4=440 Hz for nominal pitch-to-Hz calculations; alternate tunings may be applied by the composition engine.
governing_rule: Instrument identity is not a waveform label. Render from researched range + excitation method + spectral/resonance behavior + time envelope + technique + sample provenance.

reference_only_until_license_review: libraries that allow musical use but restrict redistribution of raw samples
asset_policy.do_not_assume: A web-downloadable sample is not automatically distributable inside the program.

source_hierarchy: Production references used only as secondary engineering guidance

sources.name: University of New South Wales Music Acoustics
sources.notes: University research site covering spectra, resonances, impedance, string, wind, brass, guitar, violin and didgeridoo acoustics.

sources.name: Vienna Symphonic Library Academy / Instrumentology
sources.notes: Ranges, sound production, register character, performance techniques, damping, articulation and orchestral practice.

sources.name: University of Iowa Musical Instrument Samples
sources.license: Site states recordings may be downloaded and used for any projects without restrictions.
sources.notes: Chromatic note-by-note recordings, often pp/mf/ff, with some alternate techniques; widely used in published research.

sources.name: VSCO 2 Community Edition
sources.notes: Raw WAV and SFZ orchestral material; suitable for building custom instruments.

sources.name: Versilian Community Sample Library
sources.notes: Over 4,000 samples; includes didgeridoo, bass drums, snares, toms, hi-hat, marimba, cymbals, timpani, conga family, darbuka, frame drums and more.

sources.name: Sound On Sound — Synthesizing Drums: The Bass Drum
sources.notes: Discusses coupled bass-drum modes; example orchestral partials near 50, 93, 136 and 179 Hz, plus dense mid-frequency partials and pitch decay.

sources.name: Russell & Haveman — Acoustic and modal analysis of an African djembe drum
sources.notes: JASA abstract reports djembe shell/cavity/membrane coupling and a strong Helmholtz bass component around 75 Hz.

sources.name: HyperPhysics — Acoustic Guitar
sources.notes: Standard six-string tuning E2 A2 D3 G3 B3 E4 at A440.

sources.name: Standard Bass Tuning Reference
sources.notes: Standard 4-string bass tuning E1 A1 D2 G2 at A440.

sources.name: Berklee College of Music — Writing for Big Band
sources.notes: Big-band writing treats trumpets, trombones, saxophones/selected woodwinds, and rhythm section as distinct sections.

sources.name: Library of Congress — Bluegrass Music
sources.notes: Bluegrass string-band instrumentation includes guitar, double bass, fiddle, five-string banjo, mandolin, steel guitar/Dobro; players take turns on lead.

sources.name: FreePats — Tenor Saxophone
sources.notes: CC0 tenor saxophone SFZ/SF2 assembled from VCSL samples; resource candidate, not installed by this record.

sources.name: Versilian Studios / Karoryfer — Virtuosity Drums
sources.notes: Open-source SFZ jazz drum library with auxiliary bongo, conga, timbale, agogo, shaker, claves and other percussion; resource candidate, not installed by this record.

sources.name: Country Music Hall of Fame — History of Country Music Instruments
sources.notes: Documents pedal steel, fiddle, bass, acoustic/electric guitar, piano and other country instrument roles; pedal steel uses pedals/mechanism to alter pitches and smoothly voice/modulate chords.

sources.name: University of Michigan LACS — Samba Residency
sources.notes: Demonstrates samba timeline, surdo pulse, pandeiro subdivisions, tamborim, agogo and shaker roles.

sources.name: Smithsonian Folkways — Dança! Movement and Music of Brazil
sources.notes: Describes carnival samba bateria roles including pandeiro, agogo, ganza, caixa, cuica, repinique and surdo.

instruments.name: Orchestral / Concert Bass Drum
instruments.sound_production: Large soft beater strikes batter head; two heads, shell and enclosed air are coupled resonators.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Low quasi-harmonic/inharmonic coupled modes; Sound On Sound example partials ~50, 93, 136, 179 Hz plus dense 250 Hz–1 kHz inharmonic content. VSL emphasizes indefinite pitch and very deep resonance.
instruments.time_behavior: Attack is brief/noise-like; resonance decays after strike. VSL reports resonance around 3–4 s at mezzoforte, but short notes are damped and center strikes reduce resonance.
instruments.implementation_guidance: Model as strong initial thump + decaying modal tail, not sustained sine. Separate drum resonance from room reflections.

instruments.name: Snare Drum
instruments.sound_production: Batter and snare heads coupled through shell/air; snares vibrate sympathetically against lower head.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Dense inharmonic partials/noise-like spectrum; snares add bright metallic hissing/crisp component. Sound On Sound notes low drum modes including examples near ~180 and ~330 Hz before snare contribution.
instruments.time_behavior: Very fast attack; short single-stroke decay unless rolled; snare-wire response extends/bristles after membrane strike.

instruments.name: Suspended Cymbal / Cymbal
instruments.sound_production: Metal plate struck with stick/mallet; pair cymbals use glancing plate-to-plate impact.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Broad dense inharmonic metallic spectrum rather than harmonic note series.
instruments.time_behavior: Attack can be sharp or soft depending implement; natural sustain is long unless hand/body damping is applied.

instruments.name: Timpani
instruments.sound_production: Tuned membrane over kettle resonator, struck with mallets.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Approximately harmonic tuned percussion spectrum compared with untuned drums; resonant decay is prominent.
instruments.time_behavior: Marked resonance makes rapid scales atypical; damping/secco and coperto explicitly control ring.

instruments.name: Djembe
instruments.sound_production: Goatskin membrane over open goblet-shaped cavity; shell, cavity and membrane modes couple.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Published JASA abstract reports strong Helmholtz bass component around 75 Hz; shell has bell/wineglass modes near membrane modes.
instruments.time_behavior: Different hand strokes excite different modal balances; exact attack/decay remains profile-expansion work.

instruments.name: Marimba
instruments.sound_production: Bars struck with mallets; resonators reinforce bar modes.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Tuned percussion with approximately harmonic pitch structure but bar/resonator modes shape timbre.
instruments.time_behavior: Single notes comprise attack + resonance; VSL notes low notes may ring 2–3 seconds.

instruments.name: Concert Flute
instruments.sound_production: Air jet at embouchure edge excites resonances in cylindrical air column.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Approximately complete harmonic series; soft notes approach sine-like tone, higher harmonics become stronger at higher dynamics.
instruments.time_behavior: Sustained while air is supplied; transient shaped by tongue/air attack and breath noise.

instruments.name: Clarinet in Bb
instruments.sound_production: Single reed excites approximately cylindrical bore; clarinet overblows at the twelfth.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Low/chalumeau register strongly favors odd harmonics; UNSW note spectra show first several odd harmonics stronger than even. Dynamic level changes harmonic balance substantially.
instruments.time_behavior: Sustained while blown; attack depends on tonguing and reed contact; can fade to near silence at pianissimo.
instruments.notes: Range entered from VSL register coverage; for score import preserve Bb transposition semantics separately from sounding-frequency generation.

instruments.name: Oboe
instruments.sound_production: Double reed acts as oscillating valve driving conical air column.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Low harmonics are all strong; some can exceed fundamental. UNSW gives approximate bore cutoff near 1.5 kHz; harmonics generally fall above cutoff.
instruments.time_behavior: Continuous driven tone; attack/reed transient and register strongly affect spectral character.

instruments.name: Bassoon
instruments.sound_production: Double reed drives long conical folded bore.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Low harmonics are strong; bassoon formant regions reported around 440–500 Hz and 1220–1280 Hz. Approximate bore cutoff ~600 Hz.
instruments.time_behavior: Continuous driven tone; low register full/sonorous, upper register carries fewer overtones and sounds more compressed.

instruments.name: Didgeridoo / Yidaki
instruments.sound_production: Lip vibration drives long bore; player's vocal tract strongly alters spectral envelope and formants.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: UNSW reports preferred instrument pitch range ~A1–F2; player vocal tract can create/shape strong formants, notably in ~1–2 kHz region. Tongue position can suppress around 1.5 and 2.0 kHz, leaving strong energy near ~1.8 kHz.
instruments.time_behavior: Drone is sustained by breath/circular breathing; timbre evolves continuously with tongue, glottis and vocalization.
instruments.notes: Cultural provenance should be retained; do not flatten yidaki/didgeridoo traditions into a generic effect.

instruments.name: Trumpet in C
instruments.sound_production: Lip reed excites approximately cylindrical/brass resonator; valves select different harmonic series.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Brass spectra contain a complete harmonic series structure; higher dynamics can emphasize upper partials before spectral rolloff. Narrower bore/shallow cup contributes bright high-partial content.
instruments.time_behavior: Sustained while air is supplied; fast articulated attacks possible.

instruments.name: Horn in F
instruments.sound_production: Lip reed drives long predominantly conical tube; valves select tube length/harmonic series.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Conical bore favors mellower/darker partial balance than trumpet; lowest notes respond slowly because of long air column.
instruments.time_behavior: Sustained tone; response is slower/ponderous in deepest register.

instruments.name: Tenor Trombone
instruments.sound_production: Lip reed drives long cylindrical tube; slide changes acoustic length continuously.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Brass harmonic series with strong projection; pedals E1–Bb1 are special low extension. Timbre remains relatively homogeneous across registers.
instruments.time_behavior: Sustained tone; slide travel limits some fast distant-position passages.

instruments.name: Bass Tuba
instruments.sound_production: Lip reed drives very wide conical bore; valves lengthen tube.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Wide conical bore favors deep partials and mellow spectrum; pedal tones require large airflow and are softer/ponderous.
instruments.time_behavior: Sustained while blown; lowest pedals respond with difficulty and large air demand.

instruments.name: Violin
instruments.sound_production: Bow stick-slip continuously drives string; bridge/body radiate string energy.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Rich harmonic spectrum maintained by bow. UNSW notes bridge transmits strongly around ~1–4 kHz and a broad bridge resonance around ~2.5 kHz; body has multiple resonances below 1 kHz.
instruments.time_behavior: Bowed notes sustain while energy is supplied; pizzicato decays rapidly. Bow position/pressure/speed change partial balance.

instruments.name: Viola
instruments.sound_production: Bowed/plucked strings coupled through bridge to body resonator.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Same core string physics as violin but body is proportionally small for tuning, contributing darker/statelier timbre; mute reduces higher partials above ~2 kHz per VSL.
instruments.time_behavior: Bowed sustain vs plucked decay; bow position alters brightness/partial count.

instruments.name: Cello
instruments.sound_production: Bowed/plucked strings coupled through bridge/body; four strings C2 G2 D3 A3.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Rich harmonic bowed spectrum; strong body/bridge coloration. Low C string dark/weighty, A string bright/penetrating.
instruments.time_behavior: Bowed sustain; pizzicato decays and can be strongly resonant on lower strings.

instruments.name: Double Bass
instruments.sound_production: Long bowed/plucked strings coupled through large body; standard 4-string E1 A1 D2 G2, five-string may extend to B0.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Low-frequency string spectrum with strong body radiation; bowed sound mode-locks harmonics, pizzicato retains slight inharmonicity and decays.
instruments.time_behavior: Bowed sustain; pizzicato/plucked decay; low strings slower and more massive in response.

instruments.name: Acoustic Guitar
instruments.sound_production: Plucked strings transfer energy through bridge into soundboard/body; body acts as acoustic radiator.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Plucked strings are almost harmonic but slightly inharmonic; higher-frequency components decay faster, so tone becomes mellower after the pluck. Body/soundboard resonances color different notes.
instruments.time_behavior: Sharp pluck attack followed by decaying string/body response; high harmonics decay more quickly than low components.

instruments.name: Electric Bass Guitar
instruments.sound_production: Plucked metal strings sensed by magnetic or piezo pickup and reproduced through an amplifier/speaker or modeled equivalent.
instruments.spectral_or_resonance_behavior: Strong low fundamental and lower harmonics with string/pickup harmonics above; attack brightness depends on plucking position, string type, and technique.
instruments.time_behavior: Defined pluck attack followed by controllable sustain/decay; muting shortens decay while held notes sustain through amplification.

performance_profile.clarity_rule: preserve note separation in dense rock passages

instruments.implementation_guidance: Keep the fundamental and first few harmonics clearly audible. Avoid masking the 70–180 Hz body with rhythm-guitar energy.
